QualityLayer The software factory with you in the loop 

 Plan, implement and verify software with your favorite coding agents. 
Work side by side in the App or browser, or in your own agent: terminal, IDE or agent app.

 
 
 

 
 Install •
 Workflow •
 Docs •
 Website •
 Changelog •
 Issues 
 

 
 Download the App   
 
 
 
 
 

   

 
 
 
 

 Watch the full-resolution video or try the demo in your browser. Fictional project. 

 

---

 Why QualityLayer

 “With QualityLayer, developing software with agents finally feels like doing real engineering again.”
 
 An engineer who uses QualityLayer 

 You get How it works 
 --- --- 
 Your own agent and plan Use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more with your existing login or API key. 
 A design you can review Ask your agent about diagrams and clickable screens, then approve the Plan before code changes. 
 Small, tested changes Your agent writes tests before code and hands independent parts to other agents when useful. 
 An independent check With independent review on, a separate agent checks the running change against your request before you review it. 
 Your own requirements Add checks, tools or skills to any step. Your agent records what ran, what did not, and why. Step checks. 
 Your own automations Send task events to a URL or a command, and read or start tasks from a script. Automations. 
 Visible decisions and effort Read decisions and results in your repository; see time, model usage value and cost estimates in the App. 

---

 Getting started 

 Prerequisites

- A coding agent , installed and signed in with your subscription or API key: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Antigravity, Pi, OpenCode or GitHub Copilot. Other agents connect through the CLI.
- Git and a repository.

 Installation

 Download the App and open it. Setup automatically installs the qualitylayer command (commands) and connects your agents. On a server, in WSL or in a container:

 

The App updates itself; without it, run qualitylayer update . To work on a Linux or macOS machine you reach over ssh, add it under Settings › Machines : the App installs QualityLayer there and lets you set up its agents and projects. Installation guide.

 
 Uninstalling 

 qualitylayer uninstall undoes what the installer changed; your plans stay. On Windows, even when the App is gone:

 

 

 
 Coming from Pilot Shell 11 

Run pilot update or download the App. An active Pilot Shell licence works with both products; older purchases may need help moving over. Migration and memory import.

 

 First steps

In the App or browser, choose + , then Task (Feature or Bugfix) or Chat . Pick your repository and agent, and describe what you need:

 

1. Answer questions and ask your agent to revise the Plan.
2. Approve the Plan. Your agent builds and verifies the change.
3. Review the result and recorded checks, then approve it. Ask your agent to merge, deploy or make further changes.

Prefer your terminal, IDE or agent app? Choose In my own agent , or ask there: “Using QualityLayer, plan retries for failed webhooks.” Other agents use the CLI (supported agents). Chat skips the workflow steps (Chat guide). QualityLayer runs only when you ask for it. Your first task.

 Skills your agent gets

Setup adds these skills. Ask in plain words, in any language.

 Skill For You say 
 --- --- --- 
 ql-peer Agents talking to each other “Ask Codex to review what you just built.” 
 ql-workflow Plan, implement and verify a change “Using QualityLayer, add rate limits to the export API.” 
 ql-chat Chat without workflow steps “Using QualityLayer, chat about the billing refactor.” 
 ql-artifact Designs, diagrams and pages “Open the settings design in my browser.” 
 ql-quality Code health and security scans “Scan this repository for leaked secrets.” 
 ql-manage Tasks, settings and setup “Show my open tasks.” 

More about the skills

---

 The workflow 

Three steps, two approvals. You plan and you verify; agents do everything between. Each step is one page in the App and one Markdown file in your repository, and existing plans start at Plan.

 1 · Plan, approved by you

Your agent reads the code, asks what only you can answer and writes one Plan: Done means with the steps that prove each point, named diagrams of how the change works and clickable screen previews. A bug is reproduced and diagnosed here. Plan guide

 
 
 
 

 2 · Implement, by your agents

Your agent cuts the Plan into slices and task cards, writes a failing test before each change and hands independent slices to other agents. By default it commits after each checked slice. You can choose one commit before Verify or review the checked worktree diff first. Implement guide

 
 
 
 

 3 · Verify, then approved by you

Agents that did not write the code check every point and fix what fails. Then the same page is your review: the code, the screens and each point as it ran. Verify guide

 
 
 
 

 Then the pull request. Your agent fixes failing checks and routine review threads; the task stays open until you merge. Pull request guide

 Checks and independent review

Your project's checks, code health and security scans run first. Then a separate agent reviews the change against your request. How Verify works.

 
 
 
 

 QualityLayer App

 
 
 
 

 In the App What you can do 
 --- --- 
 Chat or a planned task Talk directly with your agent or follow the workflow. See agent activity and get notified when one needs you. 
 Conversation and terminal Read the agent's conversation or its terminal beside the task. Answer questions and send quick feedback on marked text, code or artifact spots. 
 Artifacts Try clickable designs, keep them in your repository, and export designs, Plans and Reviews for teammates. Artifacts guide. 
 Checks and code review Read the evidence and file diffs, and ask your agent about any line. 
 Agent controls and usage Switch agents, choose model, effort and permissions; track limits and daily costs, including in the macOS menu bar

Prerequisites
  • A coding agent, installed and signed in with your subscription or API key: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Antigravity, Pi, OpenCode or GitHub Copilot. Other agents connect through the CLI.
  • Git and a repository.
Installation

Download the App and open it. Setup automatically installs the qualitylayer command (commands) and connects your agents. On a server, in WSL or in a container:

curl -fsSL https://qualitylayer.dev/install.sh | bash      # macOS, Linux, WSL
irm https://qualitylayer.dev/install.ps1 | iex             # Windows PowerShell

The App updates itself; without it, run qualitylayer update. To work on a Linux or macOS machine you reach over ssh, add it under Settings › Machines: the App installs QualityLayer there and lets you set up its agents and projects. Installation guide.

Uninstalling

qualitylayer uninstall undoes what the installer changed; your plans stay. On Windows, even when the App is gone:

& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://qualitylayer.dev/install.ps1))) -Uninstall
